mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives lower S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which erodes consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which reduces corporate revenue and profit growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 2% year-over-year, it signals accommodative monetary policy failing to control inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings growth expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly increase in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% signals a broad-based demand recovery, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and INDPRO both rise month-over-month by > 0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
